svg.title: The system prompt as software: five named sections
svg.desc: A hand-drawn stack of five labelled sections in fixed order: Identity, who the agent is in one paragraph; Rules, the hard constraints on what it must and must not do; Format, how outputs are shaped and which downstream code depends on; Knowledge, the small stable vital facts with everything else going to retrieval; and Tools, the catalogue with one line of usage guidance each. A panel on the right shows that only the sections a task needs enter the window on a given turn, with Identity, Rules, and Tools filled in and Format and Knowledge drawn as dashed outlines that stay out until a turn calls for them. Captions note that the boundaries between blocks are fluid, that the five are a checklist rather than a filing system, and that a prompt missing a block is not wrong provided you can say which one you left out and why.
svg.text: Five named sections in a fixed order, not freeform prose. The boundaries are fluid; load only what the task needs.
Who the agent is, in one paragraph
Hard constraints: what it must and must not do
How outputs are shaped; downstream code depends on it
Small, stable, vital facts; the rest goes to retrieval
The catalogue, with one line of usage guidance each
The boundaries are fluid. Use the five as a checklist, not a filing system, and never state one line in two blocks.
Only the sections the task needs
A prompt missing a block is not wrong, but you should be able to say which one you left out, and why.
